period: 2019 reference coverage explicitly stated on printed p1 and research question on p5; survey conducted2020, report publishedApril2021
source_locator: Peta Ekosistem Industri Game 2020, p. 34 (Sumber Daya Manusia): 1,286 workers in surveyed game developers, consisting of 1,136 at incorporated developers and 150 at unincorporated developers. Reference period: printed p1 and introductory research question; excludes Covid-impact section.
definition: Survey-respondent workforce at Indonesian video-game developers. Official study used non-probability collection: census approach for incorporated companies and community-database snowball sampling for unincorporated actors. Not a national employment estimate; worker statuses include permanent, contract and internship but the 1,286 total is not published by status. Publisher-only coverage is not established.

period: 2019 study focus; fieldwork and publication process in 2020; report published April 2021
source_locator: Peta Ekosistem Industri Game 2020, p. 34: incorporated game developers had 1,136 workers, average 35-36 per company.
definition: Component of the 1,286 survey-respondent developer total: workers at incorporated game developers only. It is the report headline number, but excludes the reported 150 workers at unincorporated developers. Non-probability study, not a national estimate. Do not sum with the all-developer total.

source_locator: Rencana Pengembangan Permainan Interaktif Nasional 2015-2019, p. 73, contribution summary item c: subsektor permainan interaktif absorbed up to 23,928 workers in 2013.
definition: National policy-document estimate for the Indonesian interactive-games creative-economy subsector. Scope is broader than video-game development: the document defines interactive games across electronic, online, physical, card and board media, and says then-available 2009 creative KBLI classifications did not fully fit its proposed scope. Do not compare with game-developer surveys.
